scope: Independent bounded source/method review; no full refit, no engine changes.

numerical_check.method: Rebuilt each saved waveform from an independent scalar-tap implementation of the documented two-piece polyBLEP formula, removed DC, and recalculated normalized residual power; no optimizer rerun.

findings.detail: The 80ms windows centered at +100ms and +160ms overlap by 882 samples (20ms, 25%). Same-note-later is partly reused training data and must not be called an independent holdout.

The one-tap full-BLEP row has freely fitted phase, gain and DC and only represents the steady mathematical oscillator. It omits the shipping filter, amp, output/capture and performance chain. It is not a production-engine baseline.

The free phase absorbs the engine Saw pre-increment convention and noncausal FIR time origin. Full conditional rank does not identify a unique physical stage, delay or oscillator algorithm; signed taps and a single periodic input preserve this ambiguity. The existing protocol explicitly records this.

The 256-point grid plus one bounded local refinement retains the observed grid solution if refinement is worse. It is a recorded bounded search, not a certificate of the global optimum for every signed-FIR family.

waveform_review: For these notes the low/high BLEP regions are disjoint. design() exactly uses 2*phase-1-polyBlep(phase,increment) at blend1, algebraically matching the free-running Saw branch. Phase absorbs the one-sample pre-increment; neither sync nor the complete engine signal path is represented.
conclusion: No blocking source, indexing or residual-calculation bug found. Interpret every candidate as exploratory effective waveform identification. Separate alias errors remain necessary because strong carrier/harmonics dominate total error power.
